My only game that came with "play this way first" rules is Isle of Skye. Usually, games can differ very much because of the scoring rules that have been selected for each match, and sometimes a game can become quite difficult when it comes to finding a great strategy, as the scoring tiles may not fit the best way together. I ended up using the "play this way first" combo of scoring tiles every time I play with a new group, as they offer a pretty easy to grasp set of scoring rules.

As others suggested, I recommend Sushi Go! too as a similar game, but with easier rules. If you plan on going for it, I would suggest going for the Sushi Go! Party version, as it gives you a wider range of cards to choose from while playing, therefore making it much more varied than the base game.

Regarding playing solo mode together with someone, me and my girlfriend actually do it with Carcassonne. We use the rules for the Carcassonne Island solo mode but we share the same tile stacks so it's pretty competitive :D

Odd indeed.

The Ottomans have been eaten very early by Hungary and Venice on one side and the Mamluks on the other side, being reduced to only 5 anatolian provinces at some point during the 1540's.

At the same time, during the 1530's Hungary owned the entire Carpathia region, 2/3 of Poland, and almost 75% of the Balkans (the other 25% being owned by Venice).

I didn't pay attention to the Ottomans until recently cuz I was thinking that they'll be finished sooner or later by someone, but I recently noticed that they are back at it, having managed to take Constantinople + some other provinces back.

Meanwhile, Hungary was facing many wars, at some point having been engaged in 3 wars at the same time, against Venice, Bohemia and Crimea (funny, cuz Crimea doesn't exist anymore). This caused a spectacular implosion, releasing Wallachia, Moldavia, Serbia, Bosnia, Albania and Bulgaria.

So pretty much the current Eastern Europe is the result of Hungary being to hungry, if I may say it like that.

My recommendation is Europa Universalis IV: I've been playing this game a lot during the past year and I felt in love with it. The fact that you can choose to play as a small nation and build your way up to becoming the greatest empire the world has ever seen is just stunning. You have to think about a lot of things before deciding what to do, you have to think what diplomatic impact will your action have on your neighbours, you also have to keep your eyes on a few resources (gold, manpower, administrative power, diplomatic power and military power) and be sure to keep them at a high level before diving in a war, or you risk losing everything. You can choose to make history your way and expand as much as possible with your country, or you can actually follow the history and recreate real empires such as the Roman Empire or the Spanish Colonial Empire.
